Chapter 23

Reads: query, batch and prerender

The store returns Published records with real patterns inside; the .remote.ts file turns them into query, query.batch for thirty cards in one request, and prerender for the featured strip computed at build time.

By the end of this chapter

Write a remote query with a valibot argument, know when query.batch turns N requests into one, and know what prerender leaves out of the server bundle.

Two files. src/lib/server/patterns.ts talks to the table and returns the shape the app uses — a Published record with a real Pattern in it, not a row with a JSON string. src/lib/remote/patterns.remote.ts exposes those to the browser, one function at a time, each with its argument validated on the way in.

withArtist is a with: clause reused by every read, so a pattern always arrives with its artist’s id and handle and nothing else about them. resolveVanity is one join — handle plus slug to id — and is what the reroute hook asks (ch. 26).

The remote file

query(schema, fn): the schema is valibot — SvelteKit accepts anything that implements Standard Schema — and the argument the function receives is the schema’s *output* type. getPattern throws a 404 with error(), so the page that calls it does not have to. getMine takes no argument and reads the cookie through currentArtist().

Thirty cards, one request

Why query.batch

A gallery page renders thirty cards and each one calls getCounts(id). Without batching that is thirty requests. query.batch tells SvelteKit to collect every argument used during one render, call the function *once* with all of them, and hand each caller its own answer through the lookup the function returns. The store’s countsFor is one WHERE id IN (...) query. Nothing in the cards changes — they still call getCounts(id) — which is the whole point.

Computed at build time

The featured strip on the landing page changes when the app is deployed and not before. prerender runs the function during the build and writes the result as a static file; the landing page, itself prerendered, reads that file. With no argument there is one possible call, so dynamic: true is absent and the function is left out of the server bundle entirely.

Checkpoint

  • You can say what type the argument of getPatterns has, and where that type came from.
  • You can explain what changes for the caller when a query becomes a query.batch — and what does not.
  • You can say when a prerendered remote function is re-run.
